reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides an instructional explanation of ways to order replacement checks through an ordinary banking process. It discusses using a voided check or account and routing information, but does not show the creator collecting or submitting that information, and the third-party search results are presented as vendor options. Possible affiliate compensation is disclosed, which provides commercial context but does not by itself establish deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: I'm going to show you three ways that you can order them.
The second way that you can order checks is going to be by calling the customer service number for Creditsuce.
The third and final way to order checks is going to be to go to Google.com and do a search for order replacement checks for Credit Seuss Bank.
what this does is it brings up several third-party vendor websites that you can order checks from
Before we get started, you will need to have a copy of a voided cheque, or something else that has your creditSeuss bank account number and routing number on it.

opening.argument: The clearest solicitation is not merely an incidental product mention: viewers are offered a concrete $5 benefit in exchange for using the creator's Cash App code. That is a low-effort reward tied directly to a viewer action, placed alongside instructions and links that encourage viewers to engage with the creator's recommended services. The check-ordering theme therefore also serves as a channel for directing viewers toward external participation and a promised cash benefit.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material instructional does not remove the explicit reward solicitation. The defense identifies how checks may be ordered, but its cited quotations do not explain why a $5 Cash App offer and an external claim link appear with that subject. The disclosure of possible affiliate compensation also confirms that the presentation is commercially directed, rather than purely neutral instruction.

citations.quote: Try Cash App using my code and we'll each get $5!
Affiliate Disclosure: I may earn a commission for my endorsement, recommendation, testimonial, and/or link to any products or services from the links above

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The $5 statement does not establish that the check-ordering instruction is a scam. It describes a separate, ordinary Cash App referral and does not promise that viewers will receive money for ordering checks. The affiliate disclosure openly identifies possible compensation, while the cited check instructions do not show that the creator collects funds or misrepresents an outcome.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an easy $5 reward, an external Cash App link, a request to use a code, and instructions involving bank credentials and account identifiers. The video also directs viewers to third-party check vendors and says they must provide account information themselves. Even if each step is described casually, this combination creates a low-friction path from the video to financial-data disclosure and an external reward flow, which warrants treating the presentation as a scam solicitation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each instruction in isolation and calls the vendors mere options. That overlooks the combined pathway: the presentation supplies an external reward link while directing viewers toward services requiring sensitive banking information. Saying that no information was visibly submitted does not answer the risk created by instructing viewers to provide it themselves.

The $5 offer is explicitly framed as a Cash App code promotion, and the check instructions identify ordinary information needed to order checks. Nothing cited shows that the creator receives the account or routing information, guarantees a payout, or makes viewers use the third-party vendors.

opening.argument: The apparent how-to format functions as promotion because it repeatedly steers viewers toward actionable destinations: a bank login, customer service, third-party vendors, and a Cash App referral link. The title presents a specific branded service, while the description adds a direct $5 incentive and affiliate links. This is therefore not just neutral education; it is a promotional funnel that uses practical instructions to build trust and direct viewers toward external actions with a promised reward.

The video does more than define checks: it directs viewers to actionable online destinations, third-party sellers, and a separately incentivized external link. Its affiliate disclosure confirms that endorsements and links are part of the presentation, so the instructional role can also be a vehicle for solicitation.
